title: Answers You Can Check: Rewayaat Inside Claude and ChatGPT
summary: For students and researchers who need to know where a narration comes from. Connect Rewayaat and Claude or ChatGPT stops relying on memory and the open web: it searches all 32,519 narrations in 18 books, in Arabic or English, tells you how many it found, and links every narration it quotes to its full text on this site.

why.title: Why not just ask Claude or ChatGPT?
why.imageAlt: Asked what al-Kāfi says about the rights of the neighbour, Claude without tools said it believed the chapter has around 15 narrations but could not reliably reproduce them, and two of the narrations it offered are not in the chapter; with web search it found the chapter on one website, in paraphrase, without confirming the count. With the Hadith connector it returned all 16, reported as complete, each with al-Majlisī's grading. Asked about Āyat al-Kursī, the connector returned the 8 narrations that bear on it, in al-Kāfi and al-Tawḥīd.
points: On its own, it can't give you the chapter. Asked what al-Kāfi says about the rights of the neighbour, Claude without tools answered “around 15 narrations … I can't reliably reproduce all of them with correct numbers” — and two of the narrations it did offer are not in that chapter. The connector returns all 16, each with the Arabic, the translation and al-Majlisī's grading, and says the list is complete.

With web search, it works from other people's pages. It found the chapter on one website, in paraphrase, and could not confirm the count. For well-known sayings it leaned on encyclopedia and fatwa pages whose page numbers differ from edition to edition. The connector reads the books themselves: all 32,519 narrations, searchable by their Arabic wording as well as by translation.

It connects narrations to the Qur'an. Ask about a verse and you get the narrations that bear on it. For Āyat al-Kursī that is eight — three in al-Kāfi, five in al-Tawḥīd — including “The Kursi encompasses everything”, graded ṣaḥīḥ.

“Not found” becomes an answer. Against a defined collection, absence means something: “Seek knowledge even as far as China” is in none of these 18 books. That is never proof a saying exists nowhere else — only that these books do not contain it.
why.source: Tested on 14 September 2026 with Claude, once without tools and once with web search only. What an assistant finds on its own changes with the model; the size of a chapter does not.

highlights: Search the full corpus by field, in Arabic or English, with the true number of matches reported so an answer can be complete rather than partial
Read a whole chapter in order, with its real size — the difference between "these appear to be the main narrations" and all seven of them
Follow the 47,522 judged similarity links between narrations, each with the reason it was judged similar
Move in both directions between narrations and the Qur'anic verses connected to them
Works with Claude and ChatGPT today, and powers the assistant on this site

guides.name: Add it to Claude
steps: Name it Hadith and paste the connector URL above. Leave Advanced settings empty — there is nothing to sign in to.
In a chat, open + → Connectors and switch Hadith on, then ask your question.
guides.note: Works on every Claude plan; the free plan allows one custom connector. On Team and Enterprise, an owner adds it once under Organization settings → Connectors.
guides.videoTitle: Adding the Hadith connector in Claude

guides.name: Add it to ChatGPT
steps: In chatgpt.com, open Settings → Apps → Advanced settings and turn on Developer mode.
Click Create app. Name it Hadith, paste the connector URL above, and set Authentication to No Auth.
Confirm that you trust the app, then click Create.
In a chat, open + and choose Hadith, then ask your question.
guides.note: Developer mode is available on the web for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu plans.
guides.videoTitle: Adding the Hadith connector in ChatGPT
